evals.prompt:
Trying to upgrade symfony/http-client to 7.x on our app and composer is dying. Here's the error:

```
Your requirements could not be resolved to an installable set of packages.

  Problem 1
    - Root composer.json requires symfony/http-client ^7.0
    - symfony/http-client[v7.0.0, ..., v7.1.3] require symfony/http-foundation ^7.0

    - symfony/serializer[v7.0.0, ..., v7.1.3] require php ^8.2

```

We're on PHP 8.1. I'm not sure if I should try to upgrade PHP or find a workaround. How do I figure out the full picture of what's blocking this?
evals.expected_output: Guidance to use `composer why-not` to trace blockers (e.g. `composer why-not symfony/http-client 7.0` and `composer why-not php 8.2`). Should identify the two distinct blockers: php version (8.1 vs required 8.2) and transitive deps. Should explain the options: upgrade to PHP 8.2 or stay on symfony 6.x. Should suggest checking what other packages block PHP 8.2 with `composer why-not php 8.2` and explain the platform config option for testing. Should NOT just say 'upgrade PHP' without showing the diagnostic steps.

assertions.name: why-not-command-mentioned
assertions.description: `composer why-not` is mentioned as a diagnostic tool to understand blockers

assertions.name: php-version-identified-as-blocker
assertions.description: PHP 8.1 vs PHP 8.2 requirement is explicitly identified as one of the blockers

assertions.name: multiple-options-presented
assertions.description: Both paths are presented: upgrading PHP to 8.2 vs staying on Symfony 6.x (not just one option)

assertions.name: diagnostic-first-not-prescriptive
assertions.description: Suggests running diagnostic commands before prescribing a solution, rather than jumping straight to 'upgrade PHP'

evals.prompt: Ugh, I just merged main into my feature branch and now composer.lock has a huge merge conflict. My branch added some new packages and main also had some updates. I don't want to just pick one side and lose changes from the other. What's the right way to handle this?
evals.expected_output: Should explain that composer.lock is generated and shouldn't be manually edited. Should direct the user to use `python3 scripts/diff_lock.py --conflict --format=summary` to understand what changed on each side, then `python3 scripts/diff_lock.py --conflict` to generate the composer require/remove commands to reconcile both sides. Should cover the basic steps: accept one side's composer.json, run the diff_lock script, apply the generated commands, then commit. Should NOT tell the user to just re-run `composer install` (which won't resolve the conflict).

assertions.name: diff-lock-script-mentioned
assertions.description: `diff_lock.py` or `scripts/diff_lock.py` is mentioned as the tool to use

assertions.name: composer-lock-is-generated
assertions.description: Explains that composer.lock is a generated file and should not be manually edited to resolve conflicts

assertions.name: no-composer-install-as-fix
assertions.description: Does NOT suggest `composer install` as the way to resolve the conflict (it won't work)

assertions.name: conflict-flag-used
assertions.description: The `--conflict` flag for diff_lock.py is shown or the workflow uses git to extract both sides

evals.prompt:
Haven't updated our packages in about 6 months, finally have some time. Here's composer outdated:

```
Package                    Current  Latest  Description
carbon/carbon              2.62.1   3.2.0   A simple PHP API extension for DateTime
doctrine/dbal              3.6.7    4.0.1   Database Abstraction Layer
guzzlehttp/guzzle          7.8.0    7.8.2   Guzzle is a PHP HTTP client library
monolog/monolog            2.9.3    3.6.0   Sends your logs to files, sockets, inboxes, HipChat...
nelmioapidocbundle/...     4.17.2   4.18.0  Generate a decent API doc
phpunit/phpunit            9.6.17   11.2.0  The PHP Unit Testing framework
ramsey/uuid                4.7.5    4.7.6   A PHP library for generating universally unique identifiers
symfony/console            6.4.1    7.1.3   Symfony Console Component
spatie/laravel-permission  5.11.0   6.4.0   Associate users with roles and permissions
```

This is a production Laravel app. Where do I start and what's safe to batch together?
evals.expected_output: Should triage the output by risk level: patch-only updates (ramsey/uuid, guzzlehttp/guzzle, nelmio) are safe to batch together; major version bumps (carbon 2→3, doctrine/dbal 3→4, monolog 2→3, spatie 5→6, phpunit 9→11, symfony 6→7) each need their own upgrade workflow with testing. Should recommend running `composer audit` first to check for CVEs. Should advise using `--dry-run` before committing to any update. Should suggest starting with the patch-only batch, then tackling major upgrades one at a time in dependency order. Should NOT recommend running `composer update` on everything at once.

assertions.name: composer-audit-first
assertions.description: Recommends running `composer audit` as a first step before starting any upgrades

assertions.name: patch-updates-identified-as-batchable
assertions.description: Identifies patch/minor updates (guzzle 7.8.0→7.8.2, ramsey/uuid 4.7.5→4.7.6) as safe to batch together

assertions.name: major-updates-flagged-as-individual
assertions.description: Flags major version bumps (carbon 2→3, doctrine 3→4, monolog 2→3, etc.) as needing individual handling with testing

assertions.name: no-update-all-at-once
assertions.description: Does NOT suggest running `composer update` without package names to update everything at once

assertions.name: dry-run-suggested
assertions.description: `--dry-run` flag is mentioned for previewing changes before applying them
